kuchen: Any of several types of cake, typically eaten with coffee.
kuching: The capital city of Sarawak, Malaysia.
kudu: A large, striped, African antelope of the species Tragelaphus imberbis (lesser kudu) or Tragelaphus strepsiceros (greater kudu).
kudzu: An Asian vine (several species in the genus Pueraria, but mostly Pueraria montana var. lobata, syn. Pueraria lobata in the US), grown as a root starch, and which is a notorious invasive weed in the United States.
A starch extracted from the root that is used in traditional East Asian medicine and cuisine.
kudzu powder: Synonym of kudzu (“a starch extracted from the root that is used in traditional East Asian medicine and cuisine”)
kulak: A prosperous peasant in the Russian Empire or the Soviet Union, who owned land and could hire workers.
kullu: A district of Himachal Pradesh, India.
kun: In the Japanese language, the pronunciation, or reading, of a kanji character as a native Japanese word that means what the character represents, contrasted with on.
kunlun: A mountain range in China forming the border between the Tarim Basin to its north and the Tibetan Plateau to its south, extending across the Chinese autonomous regions of Xinjiang and Tibet and province of Qinghai.

A mythical mountain or mountain range somewhere west of the North China Plain believed to be the home of Xiwangmu and the Peaches of Immortality, as well as other gods and Taoist immortals, and previously believed to help support the dome of the sky.
kunming: A prefecture-level city, the provincial capital of Yunnan, in southwestern China.
kunshan: A county-level city of Suzhou, Jiangsu, China.
kupiansk: Town in Kharkiv Oblast in eastern Ukraine.
A city, the administrative centre of Kupiansk urban hromada, Kupiansk Raion, Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine, founded in 1655.

A raion of Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine, established in March 1923, subordinate to the okruha of the same name of the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic until June 1930, and considerably enlarged in July 2020.
An urban hromada of Kupiansk Raion, Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine, established in June 2020.
kuqa: A county-level city of Aksu prefecture, Xinjiang autonomous region, China, formerly a county.
kurd: A member of the linguistically and culturally distinct people who speak Kurdish and mainly inhabit those parts of Turkey, Iran, Iraq and Syria sometimes known as Kurdistan.
kurdish: Family of Indo-Iranian languages of Kurdistan (in the Mesopotamia region, from the Zagros of mid-western Iran to the eastern extension of the chain of the Taurus Mountains).
Of, from, or pertaining to Kurdistan, the Kurdish people or the Kurdish language family.
kurdistan: Geographic region in the Middle East.
A cultural region in West Asia inhabited mostly by the Kurds, encompassing parts of Turkey, Iraq, Iran and Syria.
An autonomous region in northern and northeastern Iraq, lying within the aforementioned Kurdish-majority region.
A province in northwestern Iran, lying within the aforementioned Kurdish-majority region.
kursk: An impact crater in Kursk Oblast, Central Federal District, Russia, six kilometres in diameter, formed 330 to 170 million years ago.
A village, the administrative centre of Kursky selsoviet, Kulundinsky Raion, Altai Krai, Siberian Federal District, Russia, founded in 1909.
A magnetic anomaly in Chernozemye, Russia, first discovered in 1773, the largest magnetic anomaly on Earth.
A hamlet in Krasnoturansky Raion, Krasnoyarsk Krai, Siberian Federal District, Russia.
